identity.title: Cracking the Code of Juxtaposition: Can AI Models Understand the Humorous Contradictions

problem.claim: Assess whether large vision-language models can recognize and interpret humorous contradictions in two-panel comics with nonlinear or contradictory narratives.

gap.claim: Existing models are described as still struggling with the nuances of humor conveyed through juxtaposition, especially nonlinear narratives.

contributions.claim: Introduces the YesBut benchmark, with tasks spanning literal content comprehension to deep narrative reasoning for contradictory comics.
Evaluates recent commercial and open-source large vision-language models on the benchmark and analyzes their handling of narrative humor.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they introduce YesBut as a benchmark specifically targeting humorous contradictions in comics across varying difficulty levels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that even state-of-the-art models still struggle with the task.
The authors report that their experimentation and analysis provide insights into current limitations and potential improvements for AI understanding of human creative expressions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large vision-language models have broad capabilities but struggle with humor through juxtaposition and nonlinear narratives.
The study focuses on two-panel comics whose contradictory narratives create humor.
YesBut operationalizes the challenge through tasks ranging from literal comprehension to deep narrative reasoning.
Commercial and open-source models are analyzed; the authors report persistent difficulty, including for state-of-the-art systems.

source_observation.claim: The abstract organizes evaluation tasks along a difficulty range from literal content comprehension to deep narrative reasoning.

lessons.interpretation: A capability claim becomes more informative when it distinguishes surface understanding from the deeper reasoning required by the target phenomenon.
lessons.application: Define benchmark tiers that separate literal recognition from interpretation of contradiction, narrative structure, and implied humor.
lessons.exception: This tiering may be unsuitable when the task has no meaningful progression from surface processing to higher-level interpretation.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative results, model-by-model scores, baselines, or task-specific failure rates.
The exact benchmark composition, annotation process, difficulty definitions, and reported improvement directions are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independently verified validity, reproducibility, or priority over prior benchmarks.
